# Preface

This book documents Stage 2 of the Computational Language Technologies project at HSLU, building on the data pipeline and exploratory analysis completed in Stage 1.

## Dataset

The AI Media Dataset (Kaggle) consists of 16,317 news articles covering artificial intelligence topics, collected between September 2024 and August 2025.

## Stage 2 Overview

Stage 1 produced cleaned article and chunk data, sentiment labels, BERTopic topic assignments, and a knowledge graph. Stage 2 focuses on text embeddings and their evaluation:

- **Part I – Data Preparation:** Re-tokenization, train/test splits for sentiment and topic classification, and preparation of the LLM fine-tuning dataset.
- **Part II – Classical Embeddings:** Training and intrinsic evaluation of Word2Vec and FastText models on the article corpus.
- **Part III – LLM Fine-Tuning:** Supervised fine-tuning of a small open-source language model for sentiment classification.
- **Part IV – Evaluation:** Extrinsic comparison of all embedding approaches on sentiment and topic classification tasks.

## Use of AI Tools

Throughout this project, generative AI tools were used to support several parts of the workflow.

AI was used for debugging Python code, resolving library-specific questions (SentenceTransformers, LoRA), advising on architectural decisions such as the training of finetuning best-practices, and reviewing pull requests. AI also supported the writing of explanatory text throughout the notebook to ensure clarity and grammatical correctness, as this report is written in English as a non-native language.

AI was also used during active coding sessions to accelerate boilerplate code generation, particularly for data transformation steps and visualization code.

It is important to note that AI tools occasionally produced ambiguous or inconsistent answers, particularly for complex pipeline logic or edge cases in library APIs. All outputs were critically reviewed, and final decisions — including analytical interpretations, entity label choices, and topic assignments — were made manually by the team.
